title: Vocabulary app with Qwen tutoring shows a short-term score advantage in eight classes
summary: A twelve-week teaching study randomized four matched pairs of university tutorial classes to a vocabulary application or non-adaptive word lists. The application bundled Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct examples, wav2vec2.0 pronunciation feedback and rule-based review scheduling. Among 92 completers from 100 allocated students, class-adjusted posttest scores favored the application by 6.6 points on a 100-point test (95% CI 1.3–11.9). This is a prospective comparison of the complete instructional package, not an isolated effect of AI. Eight classes, repeated test items, complete-case analysis and no delayed-retention measure limit generalization.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; wav2vec 2.0 speech model; VocabPilot EDU 2.1.4

evidence.tested: March–June 2025 twelve-week application use after matched-pair class allocation, followed by week 12 testing. 100 students allocated, 92 analyzed (46 per condition); eight classes with four per arm. A class-random-intercept model estimated 6.6 points adjusted advantage, 95% CI 1.3–11.9, p=.022.
evidence.unknown: The complete package includes deterministic scheduling, mobile delivery, language-model dialogue and speech feedback; the contribution of each component was not isolated. Same-item pre/post testing, only eight clusters, attrition and self-reported control study time constrain inference. Long-term retention and transfer to broader language performance were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: A fixed named Qwen instruction model generated target-word examples/explanations, with output checks and instructor audits; a local wav2vec2.0 acoustic model supplied pronunciation practice feedback. The scheduling/recommendation rules themselves are not learned AI.

source_review.scope: Independently recovered 24-page primary publisher PDF; read allocation, named model/intervention, measures/procedure, reported adjusted results and limitations. Original article publication metadata and publisher indexed journal peer-review statement checked. No raw-data reanalysis.
